notes: Restoring a backup then rebooting came back with the old data, because this process still held the OLD file handle after restore overwrote router.db -- persist writes now freeze from the moment a restore lands until the reboot. The command log is out of the database entirely, into a rotated file: a router with a handful of PPPoE sessions had a 7MB database that was nearly all log, and that table rode along in every backup. Bulk client delete now releases DHCP leases together at the end, instead of leaving them for the five-second scan to resurrect the same clients as new. A failing persist write now shows in red on the Info tab instead of only in a log line. Assigning one shared proxy to many clients at once no longer fails for most of them (a real create-race, reproduced and fixed). Bulk delete/paste-import in the proxy pool no longer redoes a full nftables resync per item, which was the road to timeouts at a few hundred proxies.
